vulnerability.impact: Drupalgeddon2 unauthenticated remote code execution through Form API render arrays

entry_points: _drupal_bootstrap_configuration() (includes/bootstrap.inc line ~2632 in fixed 7.58) - 7.57 does not sanitize request arrays before Drupal core consumes them
request arrays (//) whose keys begin with # reach Form API/render arrays and are interpreted as render properties (#post_render etc.)
ground_truth.fix_commit: 2266d2a83db50e2f97682d9a0fb8a18e2722cba5 (SA-CORE-2018-002; adds includes/request-sanitizer.inc and requires it from _drupal_bootstrap_configuration), the sole security commit between Drupal 7.57 and 7.58. Pinned snapshot drupal-7.57 is vulnerable.
ground_truth.affected_range: Drupal 7.x before 7.58 (also Drupal 8.x before 8.3.9 / 8.4.6 / 8.5.1 for the same advisory; this card is the Drupal 7 line).
ground_truth.finding_match_rule: TP: report identifies that request parameters with keys beginning with # (e.g. #post_render, #type, #markup) are accepted into Drupal arrays and later interpreted by Form/render API, names CVE-2018-7600 (Drupalgeddon2 / SA-CORE-2018-002), and attributes unauthenticated remote code execution. Findings about Drupalgeddon3 (SA-CORE-2018-004) or unrelated XSS are not TP.
ground_truth.safe_reproduction_predicate: Static predicate: 7.57 bootstrap does not strip #-prefixed keys from request arrays; 7.58 adds DrupalRequestSanitizer::sanitize(). Dynamic reproduction: run Drupal 7.57 in a disposable container with a local SQLite DB and issue the canonical form request with a benign #-key payload that only triggers a marker callback or harmless output; no destructive commands or writes outside the sandbox.
